scope: Fresh public-source reconnaissance only. No Ox Alpha calls, no OpenRouter integration, no API keys, no external upload of ESSA source/data.

summary.currentConclusion: Ox Alpha was a short-lived stealth/preview alias. As of this research, OpenRouter identifies it as Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash, and the live OpenRouter models API lists z-ai/glm-5.3-flash rather than stealth/ox-alpha.
summary.recommendedEssaStatus: Do not integrate Ox Alpha alias. Keep GLM-5.3-Flash in Tech Radar as WATCH/RESEARCH ONLY until data handling, provider routing, pricing stability, and independent benchmark reproducibility are revalidated.

sources.title: OpenRouter Ox Alpha model page
sources.evidence: States Ox Alpha was developed and operated by ZAI, revealed as ZAI GLM-5.3-Flash; also preserves earlier stealth-language, 1M context, release Aug 20, 2026, and prompt/completion retention notice.

sources.title: OpenRouter GLM-5.3-Flash page
sources.evidence: Lists current model id z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, release Aug 26, 2026, pricing, discount through Sept 9, providers, modalities, context, max output, tools, and structured-output limitations.

sources.title: OpenRouter models API
sources.evidence: Current metadata lists z-ai/glm-5.3-flash with text+image+video input, text output, context_length 1,310,720, top_provider context 1,048,576, max_completion_tokens 131,072, supported tools and structured_outputs. No current stealth/ox-alpha entry was found in the fetched model list.

sources.title: Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash announcement
sources.evidence: Z.ai announces GLM-5.3-Flash as first natively multimodal GLM-5 model, 320B total/18B active, hybrid sparse+linear attention, 30T multimodal pretraining corpus, served during prior week on Chinese AI chips, and available on Z.ai, ZCode, and Hugging Face.

sources.title: Hugging Face model card: zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash
sources.evidence: Official Z.ai org model card with MIT license, safetensors, 321B params, text-generation usage examples, SGLang/vLLM deployment pointers, model-introduction and benchmark footnotes.

sources.title: OpenCode models documentation
sources.evidence: OpenCode states it uses AI SDK and Models.dev, supports 75+ providers and local models, but current recommended models list does not include Ox Alpha.

sources.title: OpenCode Zen documentation
sources.evidence: Current Zen endpoint table still shows 'Ox Alpha Free' with model id x-preview-f-free; OpenCode privacy section claims most Zen providers use zero-retention/no-training except listed exceptions, and Ox Alpha is not listed among exceptions.

sources.title: OpenCode Data: unknown/ox-alpha
sources.evidence: Lists ox-alpha under Unknown with rank, token usage, zero spend, and many metadata fields as Unknown.

sources.title: OpenRouter Stealth Program EULA
sources.evidence: Stealth models may be free for limited periods to collect user content; OpenRouter may share user content with stealth providers for training/improvement; stealth models can be removed anytime.

sources.title: OpenRouter Privacy Policy
sources.evidence: OpenRouter transmits inputs to selected/routed model providers; providers have differing retention/training practices; OpenRouter says it does not use inputs/outputs for model training.

sources.title: Z.ai Terms of Use
sources.evidence: For individual users, Z.ai reserves rights to process user content for service improvement/development; for API services, it says user content is not used for developing/improving services unless explicitly agreed.

sources.title: Z.ai Privacy Policy and API DPA
sources.evidence: Personal data retention varies; API DPA says Company acts as processor and, for API Section 4(b), does not store content provided/generated while using API services, processing it in real time.

sources.title: Business Insider report on Z.ai reveal
sources.evidence: Reports Z.ai confirmed Ox Alpha was an anonymous trial version of GLM-5.3-Flash released on OpenRouter/OpenCode for feedback.

sources.title: OpenCode GitHub issue #45286
sources.evidence: Community issue says z-ai/glm-5.3-flash should be added and that it replaces the well-known stealth/ox-alpha which is gone.

sources.title: Community/social mirrors of OpenCode posts
sources.evidence: Mirrored social posts claim Ox Alpha was free for a week, 1M context, multimodal, zero retention, generous limits, and 100T tokens/day capacity. Useful but not authoritative.

claims.claim: Ox Alpha currently exists as a listed historical/redirect-style OpenRouter page, but the live model identifier to use now is z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, not stealth/ox-alpha.
conflicts: OpenCode Zen docs still list Ox Alpha Free as x-preview-f-free.
unknowns: Whether OpenCode's x-preview-f-free still routes successfully today was not tested because that would require provider/API use.
requiresRevalidation: Before any ESSA design update, re-fetch OpenRouter models API and OpenCode Zen models endpoint.

claims.claim: Exact current model identifier on OpenRouter is z-ai/glm-5.3-flash; old alias was stealth/ox-alpha.
requiresRevalidation: Model IDs can change; verify at implementation time.

claims.claim: Developer/operator identity is now officially confirmed as Z.ai/ZAI by OpenRouter and Z.ai materials; earlier anonymity/speculation is obsolete for current status.
conflicts: Older Aug 22-24 articles correctly described the developer as unknown at that time.
unknowns: Exact contractual subprocessor chain during stealth preview remains only partly visible.

claims.claim: Ox Alpha first appeared/released on OpenRouter on Aug 20, 2026; GLM-5.3-Flash was released Aug 26, 2026.

Ox Alpha/OpenRouter preview was free; current GLM-5.3-Flash is paid on OpenRouter at $0.15/M input and $0.50/M output standard, with $0.075/M input and $0.25/M output discount through Sept 9, 2026 16:00 UTC on listed discounted providers.
conflicts: Older preview pages/articles say free; that was time-bound and alias-specific.
unknowns: Z.ai direct pricing page may lag current release-specific pricing.
requiresRevalidation: Pricing and discount expiration must be checked live before budgeting.

claims.claim: A claim that Ox Alpha was 'free until August 27' is plausible as a one-week preview from Aug 20, but the authoritative current paid discount expiration is Sept 9, 2026 for GLM-5.3-Flash on OpenRouter.
conflicts: OpenRouter stealth EULA says limited period but does not name Aug 27; social posts say 'for the next week'/'next 6 days'.
unknowns: Exact time the free alias stopped serving for every route.
requiresRevalidation: Do not rely on any free period without live provider metadata.

claims.claim: Context window is about 1M tokens: OpenRouter page says 1M, API top provider says 1,048,576, API model context_length says 1,310,720.
unknowns: Whether every provider reliably supports full context in production.
requiresRevalidation: Use top_provider/context plus provider endpoint metadata for implementation caps.

claims.claim: Maximum output is 131,072 completion tokens on OpenRouter for GLM-5.3-Flash.
conflicts: Z.ai benchmark footnotes mention larger max generation for a specific HLE evaluation setup, not necessarily public API max output.

claims.claim: Supported API inputs on OpenRouter are text, image, and video; output is text. Audio is not listed for GLM-5.3-Flash on OpenRouter.
conflicts: Hugging Face model card currently appears under text-generation and image/text examples; OpenRouter exposes video as an input modality.
unknowns: Exact video container limits, sampling behavior, maximum duration, and whether every routed provider supports video equivalently.
requiresRevalidation: Before media use, verify provider-specific multimodal request schema and video limits.

claims.claim: Tool/function calling is supported through tools/tool_choice; structured output is partially supported via response_format/structured_outputs, but OpenRouter FAQ says JSON-schema enforcement is not supported.
conflicts: API metadata includes structured_outputs, while FAQ narrows this to response_format without schema enforcement.
unknowns: Practical reliability of tool calling and schema adherence on complex ESSA tasks.
requiresRevalidation: Run local benchmark harness only after explicit approval and without sensitive ESSA data.

claims.claim: Coding and agentic capabilities are claimed by OpenRouter, Z.ai, and OpenCode; benchmark evidence is mostly vendor/platform reported, not yet independently reproduced at large scale.
conflicts: Community posts report both strong and mixed outcomes; no fully independent ESSA-relevant benchmark was found in this research pass.
unknowns: Reliability across ESSA's production, governance, media, and property workflows.
requiresRevalidation: Treat as candidate benchmark target, not production model.

claims.claim: The model can directly accept video input via supported provider routes, but autonomous video editing/rendering is not model-native; full video production requires an agent harness plus tools such as browser/computer use, FFmpeg, renderers, or app automation.
conflicts: Viral/social claims describe full video workflows, but Z.ai's own text describes ZCode Browser Use and Computer Use as agent actions, not the model itself rendering final video.
unknowns: How well the model reasons over long video natively versus sampled frames/transcripts in each provider stack.
requiresRevalidation: Separate MODEL_CAPABILITY, AGENT_HARNESS_CAPABILITY, and EXTERNAL_TOOL_CAPABILITY in all ESSA docs.

claims.claim: Claims that Ox Alpha beats GPT-5.6 Sol or Claude Fable 5 are not verified. Z.ai's current GLM-5.3-Flash benchmark table compares against GPT-5.6 Terra and Opus 4.8, not GPT-5.6 Sol or Claude Fable 5; older GLM-5.3 page shows GLM-5.3 behind GPT-5.6 Sol and Fable 5 on DeepSWE.
conflicts: A community 10-task DeepSWE screenshot reportedly placed Ox Alpha above Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, but this is not an authoritative benchmark.
unknowns: No reproducible, public, same-harness comparison of Ox Alpha/GLM-5.3-Flash vs GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5 was found.
requiresRevalidation: Do not encode superiority claims in ESSA Tech Radar.

claims.claim: OpenRouter stealth-route data handling is conflicting: the Ox Alpha model page says prompts/completions were retained by provider and not used for training, while the generic Stealth EULA says stealth user content may be collected/shared for stealth-model training and improvement.
conflicts: Model-specific notice vs generic EULA differ on training/improvement.
unknowns: Which statement controls for the exact stealth/ox-alpha preview period and each downstream provider route.
requiresRevalidation: Require legal/security review before sending any ESSA data through OpenRouter or stealth-like routes.

claims.claim: OpenCode Zen claims zero retention/no training for providers except listed exceptions, and Ox Alpha is not listed as an exception; however OpenRouter's route had different retention terms.
conflicts: Different routes have different privacy promises.
unknowns: Whether OpenCode's current x-preview-f-free still exists and what provider agreement applied during Aug 20-27.
requiresRevalidation: Provider route must be treated as part of the model identity in ESSA.

claims.claim: Z.ai API terms distinguish individual users from API customers: individual content may be used for improvement/development; API End User Content is not used for service improvement unless explicitly agreed, and API DPA claims no storage of submitted/generated content during API service use.
conflicts: OpenRouter/OpenCode routing terms may differ from direct Z.ai API terms.
unknowns: Subprocessors for each OpenRouter provider route are not fully enumerated in the reviewed sources.
requiresRevalidation: Direct Z.ai API legal terms and any DPA must be reviewed before enterprise use.

claims.claim: Current OpenRouter routes for GLM-5.3-Flash include Z.ai, NovitaAI, GMICloud, Cloudflare, DeepInfra, io.net, and Baseten.
unknowns: Provider-specific subprocessors, regions, retention, and video support equivalence.
requiresRevalidation: Pin/exclude providers only after provider-specific security review.

claims.claim: Open weights are publicly available under MIT license on Hugging Face.
unknowns: Operational feasibility/cost of local serving for ESSA not assessed in this read-only research.
requiresRevalidation: If considering local/offline use, perform separate supply-chain, weight provenance, license, and hardware review.

claims.claim: There are security concerns relevant to ESSA: stealth alias disappearance risk, route-dependent retention/training terms, multimodal biometric/personal-data exposure, provider/subprocessor ambiguity, and cyber/malicious-code policy restrictions.
unknowns: Whether enterprise/private deployments can fully disable logging across all providers.
requiresRevalidation: No ESSA source, secrets, user media, or customer data should be sent until reviewed and approved.

claims.claim: Ox Alpha was a temporary alias/stealth evaluation model.

confirmed: Ox Alpha was the stealth/preview alias for Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash.
OpenRouter currently lists GLM-5.3-Flash as z-ai/glm-5.3-flash; Ox Alpha page exists as a revealed historical listing.
OpenRouter GLM-5.3-Flash supports text/image/video input and text output, tools/tool_choice, response_format/structured output flags, about 1M context, and 131,072 max completion tokens.
Current OpenRouter pricing is paid, with a 50% discount through Sept 9, 2026 16:00 UTC on listed discounted providers.
GLM-5.3-Flash weights are on Hugging Face under MIT license.
likely: The free preview ran approximately one week from Aug 20, 2026, making Aug 27 a plausible end date, but exact route-by-route cutoff was not verified by calling providers.
The model is strong enough to merit ESSA benchmark research, especially coding/agentic workflows, but production reliability is unproven.
unverified: Ox Alpha can perform full video-production workflows without agent/tool orchestration.
Every provider route supports video input equally and directly rather than via preprocessing.
falseOrMisleading: Calling Ox Alpha currently anonymous is outdated/misleading after Z.ai/OpenRouter reveal.
Calling video rendering/editing a native model capability is misleading; rendering/editing is an external tool or agent harness capability.
Treating OpenRouter, OpenCode, Claude Code, ZCode, FFmpeg/renderers, and Ox Alpha/GLM-5.3-Flash as one capability layer is misleading.
unknown: Exact prompt/completion retention for each historical route and provider.
Provider/subprocessor details for all current OpenRouter providers.
Provider-specific video limits and whether video understanding is native on each route.
essaRelevance: Candidate for future benchmark architecture only after route-specific security review.
Useful comparison point for long-context coding/agent tasks and multimodal reasoning, not an ESSA default model.
Any Tech Radar entry should say 'GLM-5.3-Flash, formerly Ox Alpha alias' rather than treating Ox Alpha as a stable model.
essaSecurityConcerns: Do not send ESSA source, secrets, user data, or media to stealth/unknown routes.
OpenRouter stealth terms and model-specific notices conflict enough to require review.
Multimodal inputs may include biometric/personal data; provider route must be approved before use.
Avoid claims of direct media production; keep model reasoning separate from local FFmpeg/browser/render execution.
factCheck.recommendedEssaStatus: WATCH / RESEARCH ONLY. Do not integrate the Ox Alpha alias. If Phase 21K-OX proceeds, update Tech Radar around GLM-5.3-Flash as a revalidation-gated candidate, and build benchmark architecture that can test model capability separately from agent harness and external tools.
